newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar firmer after nearby NY strength.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar firmer after nearby NY strength.

text.p: London white sugar futures perked up slightly in late afternoon trade on Tuesday as a show of strength on the raws market stirred sentiment but the turnover mostly derived from against actuals and crossed trades.
Premium selling of the spot March contract at around $70 was also noted after the move on the raws market, traders said. The August/October spread also attracted some interest.
But most of the market turnover came from crosses on the nearby positions and also the December 1997 contract so outright volume was limited, they said.
At 1750 GMT March was $1.20 higher at $304.40 and May up $1.10 at $304.70. Volume totalled 2,193 lots.
Technically, March has finally broken through its 10-day moving average and the upper limit of a downward channel in place since mid-September.
Outside the channel, the first main upside target should come from mid-month highs at $307, reinforced by the 20-day average at $306.70.

Its slow stochastic indicators have just crossed to the upside while in oversold territory, confirming the market reversal, while momentum indicators are also pointing higher. In physical news, Zimbabwe tendered to buy 28,000 tonnes of raw sugar for arrival in two shipments in January and February.

Traders said the tender had a deadline of 1700 hours local time on November 22, they said. Various shipments options were possible but the initial requirement was for two 14,000-tonne cargoes to arrive for January 6/11 and February 3/8.
In Paris all traded positions gained ground in a total volume of 439 lots. March was up $1.20 at $304.20 and May up $1.00 at $304.20.
